🤖 Holistic review of fc69cb056452e9d15f58750d8575b269f44c0ef0 (updated from 64f26a536e).

This PR adds lexical decontamination to the taskcompendium source pipeline, between filter and verification. The stage design fits the pipeline, and fc69cb0564 fixes the empty-partition crash in `_attribute`. One problem remains: the PR body still reports the run of the replaced reproduction harness, so the stated ASDiv acceptance is not tied to the code being merged.

**System**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph tc["lib/taskcompendium run_source_pipeline"]
    filter["_filter"] --> lex["decontaminate_population"]:::added
    lex -->|"checked audit (TRAIN: gated)"| verify["_verify"]:::changed
    verify --> export["_export_sidecars / _write_manifest"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph exp["experiments task_curation"]
    driver["driver --lexical-*"]:::changed --> engine["DatakitDecontamination"]:::added
    repro["lexical_reproduction"]:::added -->|"FULL run"| tc
    engine --> decon["marin.datakit.decon (hash_to_evals)"]:::changed
    engine --> fam["decontam/eval_families"]:::added
  end
  engine -. "DecontaminationEngine Protocol" .-> lex
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Why.** #12399 moves the Atlas ETL stages from `atlas-env-audit` into `run_source_pipeline`. Lexical decontamination is the first of those stages. Its acceptance test is reproducing the sealed ASDiv release.

**Design.** `SourcePipelineConfig.decontamination` holds a `DecontaminationEngine` Protocol, mirroring `Reviewer` and `GradingMachines`; taskcompendium cannot import `marin`. The stage renders each kept row with `format_conversation`, asks the engine for per-task flags, publishes `lexical/{measurement.json,task_flags,drop_manifest.parquet}`, and for TRAIN sources rewrites the filtered audit with contaminated kept rows rejected as `lexical:contaminated`. `pipeline_identity` adds a `lexical` key only when an engine is configured, with only this source's adopted drop set. The harness runs the FULL pipeline with the rubric cleared. It compares flags over `lexical/task_flags`, compares texts re-rendered from `normalize/` for the same IDs, and checks retained IDs against `final/`.

**Evidence and limits.** At fc69cb0564 these tests pass: the 5 tests in `lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_lexical_decontamination.py` and the 2 tests in the new `experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_lexical_engine.py`. The second file covers eval-ID and family attribution and the zero-row mark partition. `infra/ci/select_tests.py` selects it for this diff. Downstream readers in `lexical.py` (`contaminated_ids`, `copy_flags`, `write_drop_manifest`) handle a zero-row flags file. I did not run the ASDiv reproduction. No open PR touching these paths requires action.

**Findings**

- **2. Should fix:** The harness comparison is fixed: flags, texts and summaries now cover `set(main_flags) & set(branch_flags)`, contaminated rows included. However, the PR body, which becomes the squash commit message, still credits the acceptance to "rebuilt main's census from the registered converter" and to job `/benfeuer/lexical-reproduction-asdiv-5`. Both describe the harness that d99e599894 replaced. Rerun the current harness and replace the acceptance numbers, artifact URL and job with that run's results.

Earlier findings: 3 and 4 resolved at 64db3e6426, 5 resolved at 64f26a536e. 6 resolved; `_attribute` writes `TASK_FLAGS_SCHEMA.empty_table()` for a zero-row mark file, and `test_attribute_keeps_a_flag_file_for_a_zero_row_mark_partition` covers it.

🤖 The 410 ASDiv tasks this stage admits are `asdiv` evaluation items. ASDiv.xml at the pinned revision holds the same 2,305 problems, in the same order, as `EleutherAI/asdiv` (validation). `experiments/evals/task_configs.py` runs that set as `asdiv_0shot`, and `prepare_eval_corpus.py` indexes it as a required task.

The counts reproduce from public data. I ran the FULL source pipeline at `fc69cb0564` with `DatakitDecontamination`, a bloom that `build_eval_bloom` built from the 2,305 `asdiv` records as `_lmh_doc_text` writes them, an empty global drop set, and the source drop set the engine builds (0 hashes). The stage measures 2,294 tasks, marks 1,884 (fraction 0.82127, mean overlap 0.75674) and admits 410, as in the PR body. Marking all 2,305 problems directly with `_document_overlap_and_matches` gives the sealed receipt's 1,895, 0.82213 and 0.75745.

The 410 are short. The task renders as `User:\n<Body>\n\n<Question>`. The indexed text is `<Body>\nQuestion:<Question>\nAnswer:`, then the target and each raw field as its own paragraph, and a short paragraph inside a longer record adds no 13-gram.

- 230 tasks have no paragraph of 13 tokens. In the record fallback every 13-gram crosses the Body/Question boundary, where the indexed text has `Question:` glued to the first word.
- 101 have a 12-token Body, so their only 13-gram starts with `User:`.
- 79 have one matching 13-gram, below `min_matched_features=2`.

Without the `User:` label, 76 of the 410 would be marked.

#11497 lists ASDiv as banned, so these 410 may never reach a training run. `numina_math` is declared a training source and carries the same items. In `AI-MO/NuminaMath-CoT` at the pinned revision, 1,329 rows of the `orca_math` subset are `asdiv` items with Body and Question joined by a space (1,208 distinct problems). I ran the stage on those rows plus the first 5,000 rows of the source, against a bloom of `asdiv` and the seven `hendrycks_math` test sets. Of the 1,213 rows that survive conversion and dedup, the stage marks 581 and admits 632 (627 distinct items, median overlap 0.27). The problem is one paragraph, and its 13-grams that cross the Body/Question boundary never match.

lm-eval's `asdiv` task declares `doc_to_decontamination_query: "{{body}} {{question}}"`, which is the form of these rows, and `_lmh_doc_text` does not index it. With that query added to each record as one more paragraph, the marking function marks 1,198 of the 1,208 distinct copies and 206 of the 410 ASDiv tasks.

One admitted item (1859) and one marked item (957), each rendered as the ASDiv source renders it, without the role label, and as one paragraph. Each line prints the item, the overlap and whether it is marked:

```python
from marin.datakit.decon import NGramConfig, _bloom_hash, _document_overlap_and_matches, _extract_features

ngram = NGramConfig(ngram_length=13, stride=0, overlap_threshold=0.5, min_matched_features=2)
items = {
    1859: ("A waiter had fourteen customers. After some left he still had three customers.",
           "How many customers left?", "11", "11 (customers)", "14-3=11", "Subtraction"),
    957: ("Zachary did 47 push-ups in gym class today. David did 15 more push-ups than Zachary.",
          "How many push-ups did David do?", "62", "62 (push-ups)", "47+15=62", "Addition"),
}
for index, (body, question, target, answer, formula, kind) in items.items():
    indexed = f"{body}\nQuestion:{question}\nAnswer:\n\n{target}\n\n{answer}\n\n{body}\n\n{formula}\n\n{question}\n\n{kind}"
    bloom = {_bloom_hash(feature) for feature in _extract_features(indexed, ngram)}
    for text in (f"User:\n{body}\n\n{question}", f"{body}\n\n{question}", f"User:\n{body} {question}"):
        score, matched = _document_overlap_and_matches(text, bloom, ngram)
        print(index, round(score, 2), bool(matched))
```

```text
1859 0.5 False
1859 1.0 True
1859 0.17 False
957 0.75 True
957 1.0 True
957 0.3 False
```

#6852 describes the low recall on short and embedded copies in general, and #11993 names ASDiv's `Question:` join for its own keys. #11993 also removes `decon_to_parquet` and `build_all_source_drop_sets`, which `lexical_engine.py` imports.

cc @chrismc91

🤖 Holistic review of 68c07d0d775bbde2a800bdd2b62e81e4715a86e2.

This change fixes the startup crash where SkyRL could not combine prompt or task input files whose text columns used different Arrow string widths. It widens top-level text columns, which covers the reported Mochi failure. The docstring and PR body now say that nested text, such as source-format `prompt` message lists, keeps its original width and still raises on mixed widths.

**Before.** `read_prompt_files` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/dataset/dataset.py`) loaded each source and passed the list straight to `datasets.concatenate_datasets`. Hugging Face `datasets` treats `Value("string")` and `Value("large_string")` as different features. So a Parquet source written with `large_string` could not be combined with one written with `string`. The run failed at startup with "The features can't be aligned". `PromptDataset`, `TaskDataset._prepare_cached_rows`, and the tokenized `PreferencePairDataset` path all read through this function.

**After.** The new `concatenate_prompt_datasets` casts every top-level `Value("string")` column to `large_string` before concatenation, including when only narrow strings are present. Other type mismatches, such as float against string, still raise `ValueError`. I ran `skyrl-train/tests/cpu/test_dataset.py` locally at `394d7d79` (the later commit edits only a docstring) with the CI extras (`uv run --frozen --extra cpu --group dev`): 22 passed. The new cases cover narrow/wide, wide/narrow, and narrow/narrow inputs and check that the JSON, hashes, routes, nulls, and floats come through unchanged. No open PR on these paths conflicts with this one.

No findings.

🤖
# Research

The lease serializes acquisition but does not fence writes: status writes replace the shared file, and a lost heartbeat raises only when `step_lock` exits. The runner passes the same output path to inline and Fray work; lazy steps and the remote wrapper can write records before the parent sees the lease loss. Refreshing before a write would narrow the window, but a takeover can still occur between the refresh and the write, and data writes can already be in flight.

**Relevant code**
- [`step_status.py#L113-L124`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L113-L124) — unconditional status replacement
- [`step_status.py#L242-L284`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L242-L284) — lease loss surfaced on exit
- [`step_runner.py#L452-L473`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L452-L473) — shared output and terminal writes
- [`step_runner.py#L490-L498`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L490-L498) — remote record write
- [`lazy.py#L336-L375`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py#L336-L375) — lazy record write

# Proposed Fix

Give each execution a unique staging directory beside its canonical output path. Pass that directory to inline functions, Fray jobs, lazy builders, and sweep cells so an old worker can finish writing only to its own attempt. Keep the canonical path as the step identity and store its lease, terminal state, and published attempt pointer in one atomically updated state object. Publishing SUCCESS or FAILED must compare the attempt's fencing token with the current owner in the same conditional write; a stale worker raises `LeaseLostError` and cannot replace the winning pointer. Use GCS generations, S3 ETags, and local file locking; fail closed on backends without an atomic conditional update.

Resolve successful dependencies and artifact reads through the published pointer, including records and returned paths. Keep a prior successful attempt readable during a mutable rerun until its replacement commits. Read existing completed directories as legacy outputs, but put new writes in attempt directories. Update `disk_cache` and sweep's direct status/record paths under the same rule.

Test a deterministic takeover: pause A, let its lease expire, let B publish success, then resume A through failure and record writes. The canonical status, record, and resolved data must still belong to B. Repeat with a Fray worker and a lazy artifact; test that a failed or abandoned attempt never becomes visible.

Open question: do any consumers require direct file access at the canonical output path without using Marin's artifact resolver? Those callers need an explicit migration because copying attempt data into that path would restore the race.

The hero-clean variant differs in its benchmark name, recipe name, protocol version, population, `SourceInfo.variant`, and an `HfSource.select` row selector, `partial(listed, question_ids=HERO_CLEAN_IDS)`. `callable_identity` (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/fingerprints.py:50`) hashes partial keywords, so the 379 IDs become part of the corpus identity, as the body says. `expected_population=379` makes a corpus build fail if an ID stops matching. - **1. Should fix:** `experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/livecodebench.py:88` The 379 IDs are the only definition of "hero-clean", and the 13-gram scan that produced them is described only in prose in #12408. No checked-in or published code or output backs it. 🤖 Holistic review of 3df02aace0a404c854c18338a7e163ba730ee950.

This change makes periodic Megatron S3 checkpoints overlap the next policy update. Each rank copies its DCP write plan into a bounded host buffer, releases the source state dictionary, and streams the copies to S3 from a background thread on a dedicated Gloo group. The trainer publishes trainer/rollout state, the resume marker, and then `on_save` only after every rank's write settles. I found nothing new to act on.

**Before.** `MegatronStrategy.save_checkpoint` ran `checkpoint.save` synchronously through `MasterWeightsWriter`, so the full S3 shard write sat inside the `save_checkpoint` actor RPC. The trainer overlapped only the small trainer-state/marker writes and fired `on_save` before starting them.

**Design.** `DirectS3TorchDistSaveShardedStrategy.save` submits `StagedMasterWeightsWriter.save` to a one-thread executor. The writer drives DCP's `_save_state_dict` directly so it owns the only state dictionary, and it clears that dictionary once staging completes. The strategy refuses flattening planners that would copy it. `_wait_for_staging` all-reduces "staged" across ranks before MCore's metadata barrier, so a failed plan or copy on any rank surfaces from `save_checkpoint` on every rank. Control files stay in a private temp directory, held by `_PendingCheckpoint`, until `finish_checkpoint` joins the write (mapping an all-`OSError` `CheckpointException` to `OSError`) and uploads them. `DistributedStrategy` declares `checkpoint_write_done` / `finish_checkpoint` / `discard_checkpoint_control_files` as idle no-ops, so the trainer runs one publication lifecycle for every backend. The budget is `trainer.policy.megatron_config.checkpoint_max_staged_host_bytes`.

The two commits since the last review change how the trainer classifies errors. `_save_intermediate_checkpoint` now enters colocated residency through `_checkpoint_policy_residency` on an `AsyncExitStack`. It registers the pending publication before inference is restored, and it raises restore failures without counting them as checkpoint save failures. Previously, an `OSError` while restoring inference was counted as a storage failure and training continued with inference not restored. Now training stops, and the shutdown drain still publishes the staged checkpoint. The publish task now handles storage `OSError` itself and returns `None`, so an `on_save` callback error propagates from the drain instead of being recorded as a failed save.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  trainer["RayPPOTrainer._save_intermediate_checkpoint"]:::changed -->|"save_checkpoint"| strat["MegatronStrategy"]:::changed
  strat --> direct["DirectS3TorchDistSaveShardedStrategy"]:::changed
  direct -->|"executor + Gloo group"| writer["StagedMasterWeightsWriter"]:::added
  writer -->|"bounded host buffer"| s3["S3 shard / .metadata"]
  publish["publish task"]:::changed -->|"poll done, finish_checkpoint"| strat
  publish -->|"after finish"| marker["trainer_state, rollout_state, latest marker, on_save"]
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Evidence and limits.** At this head, `test_best_checkpoint_selection.py` and `test_megatron_checkpoint_storage.py` pass locally in the SkyRL env (`uv run --frozen --extra cpu --group dev`, 21 tests). The publication test now covers four cases: success, a failed shard write, a failed inference restore, and a failed `on_save`. In the restore case the save raises and the staged checkpoint still publishes on drain. In the callback case the error propagates without a save-failure metric. Megatron is not installed in the CPU env, so `_wait_for_staging`, the MCore adapter, and the `FullyParallelSaveStrategyWrapper` path run only on GPU. The body records no GPU/S3 run that measures the overlap. With the default `fully_reshardable` format, DP rank 0 gathers optimizer state and can dominate the save; the body and `docs/dev-guide/skyrl.md` state this limit. `StagedMasterWeightsWriter.save` depends on DCP's private `_save_state_dict`, so a torch upgrade should rerun these tests.

No findings.

Earlier findings resolved: 1, the trainer runs one publication lifecycle with `on_save` after publication. 2, the budget lives on the policy Megatron config. 3, `test_checkpoint_publication_waits_for_policy_write` covers publication ordering and failure handling.

Pre-commit passed every check except Pyrefly, which reported missing dependencies in untouched modules. The review's design findings remain with the author.

12423.body: Working on this in loom: https://loom.oa.dev/s/5a0bu1ki

🤖 **Review: the default `empty` snapshot makes every new multi-GPU compile run at the untuned rate, and it breaks the current warm-up workaround.**

Context is issue 11775. The slow mode (about 125 s per update on the 64-H100 e12 config, against about 45 s) is untuned kernels on the ranks that fetch no tuned set.

**What changes after merge, with no `IRIS_AUTOTUNE_STORE_ROOT`**
- `_enable_shared_autotune_cache` stages `EMPTY_SNAPSHOT_ID` on every node. Nothing in the repo sets `IRIS_AUTOTUNE_STORE_ROOT` yet.
- So all 64 ranks compile untuned. Issue 11793 measured exactly this setup (one empty folder on all ranks) at 121–130 s per update in two regions.
- Today a warm-up job helps because process 0 fetches the tuned set, compiles a tuned executable, and writes it to the persistent cache. With this PR, process 0's executable is untuned too, so a warm-up then a cache hit also runs at about 125 s.
- The multi-process path also starts no uploader. So no tuned set is built up from new runs.
- Net effect: the hang goes away (one executable), but runs that are about 45 s today become about 125 s on any new cache key.

**Suggested before merge**
1. Ship a seeded tuned snapshot and set `IRIS_AUTOTUNE_STORE_ROOT` by default for the H100 GPU variant, under the compatibility key. One candidate already exists: the 246,247-file `.textproto` set staged in issue 11793. It gave one executable on 64/64 ranks and 47.9–48.9 s per step on a cold compile in read mode. It is in `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/diag-11793-uniform-tuned-02a-v4-20261120/autotune-56dcb29c80-top246247.tar.gz` (a `ttl=30d` prefix).
2. Or keep the fetched tuned set as the default input for every rank until a seeded snapshot exists, rather than `empty`.
3. Put the speed trade-off in `OPS.md`. It says `empty` "uses untuned kernels", but not that this is about 2.7x slower on the 64-H100 SFT step.

**Validation:** I plan to run this branch with a FineStore store seeded from that set: a cold compile on 64 H100 in cw-us-east-02a, 3 updates. I will report the per-rank HLO hashes and step times here.

🤖 **Partial validation on 64 H100 (cw-us-east-02a): staging works; a second `configure_jax_compilation_cache()` call now fails. Step-time result still pending.**

I ran this PR's diff, plus PR 11923's guard, on the e12 FP32 SFT launcher, with a store seeded from the 246,247-file tuned set (snapshot `58c1a2829ad24d0b96065cf55f1391ea`).

- **Staging:** the 36 ranks that logged before the failure below all reported `snapshot_id=58c1a2829ad24d0b96065cf55f1391ea file_count=246247`. So the pinned fetch and the per-node ready marker work at this scale.
- **Repeat call now fails.** The launcher called `configure_jax_compilation_cache()` itself, and then `initialize_jax()` called it again. The first call appends `--xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir=<snapshot>` to `XLA_FLAGS`. The second call then rejects that flag on every rank: `ValueError: multi-process GPU jobs cannot set a per-rank XLA autotune cache directory`.
  - On `main`, only `initialize_jax()` calls this function, so this is not a bug on `main` today.
  - Before this PR, a repeat call was a no-op, because the function returned early when the flag was already set. Consider making the shared path accept a flag that already points at this attempt's own snapshot directory.
- **Step time not measured yet.** My second attempt failed before compiling, because the e12 template's inputs under `tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/e12/` are gone (its initializer and eval caches). I will post the cold-compile step time when I have a config whose inputs still exist.

🤖 Validation of PR 12423 with a seeded tuned snapshot: the train step works, but an eval program failed.

Setup:
- Job `/karan/task504-distill-1h-a-hard-20261128c-i11775v3`: 64 H100 in 02a.
- Code: PR 12423 plus the PR 11923 compile guard.
- Compile cache: a new empty JAX cache, so every rank compiles cold.
- Autotune: snapshot `58c1a2829ad24d0b96065cf55f1391ea` (246,247 tuned files).
- Start point: the e12 base checkpoints have expired, so the run resumes a kept checkpoint of the same model and optimizer and runs 14 steps.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Snapshot staged | 64 of 64 ranks, same snapshot id, `file_count=246247` |
| Train step compile | Every train-step compile passed the cross-rank executable check, so all 64 ranks ran one executable |
| Steady train step, rank 0, steps 481–493 | 36.9–53.1 s, median about 47 s. The untuned path is about 125 s. |
| End-of-run eval (`jit_accum_for_batch`) | **Failed the guard: 13 distinct optimized-HLO hashes across 64 ranks** |

So with tuned data present, the cold-compiled train step matches the cache-hit speed. This supports the root cause posted earlier.

The eval failure is a separate open question:
- The pre-compile fingerprint check passed, so every rank gave XLA the same module.
- Every rank also read the same snapshot. Ranks on the same node, which share one staged folder, still produced different executables. For example, node 0's ranks fall into 5 hash groups.
- So uniform autotune files are not enough to make this compile deterministic.

I don't know the cause yet. My guess is that the eval fusions are not in this train-derived snapshot, and that a miss is not handled the same way on every rank, but I have not checked this. I've started a 1-step rerun with a fresh cache (`...20261128d-i11775v4`). It saves one optimized HLO per variant to S3, so the variants can be diffed directly.

Consequence for PR 12423 together with PR 11923: with a seeded snapshot, a job whose eval programs miss the snapshot fails at its first eval instead of running.

🤖 Follow-up on the eval mismatch: the cause is not autotuning.

The 1-step rerun with a fresh compile cache (`/karan/task504-distill-1h-a-hard-20261128d-i11775v4`) failed the same way on `jit_accum_for_batch`, this time with **17** distinct optimized-HLO hashes across 64 ranks. Some hashes are the same as in the 14-step run. I saved one optimized HLO per variant and compared them.

What the 17 variants show:
- **The Triton fusion configs are identical.** All 17 variants have the same 16 Triton fusions with the same block-level tile configs (ignoring stream-queue ids). So my guess that eval fusions miss the snapshot was wrong for this mismatch.
- **They diverge before scheduling.** Each variant carries a different `fingerprint_before_lhs`, so the modules already differ before the latency-hiding scheduler runs.
- **The difference is fusion structure.** It sits in small `s32[4,…]` slice/min/pad/concatenate trees in the model's mask/segment path (`jit(accum_for_batch)/Transformer/...`). Variants fuse different levels of a pairwise-min tree into a neighbouring fusion, and they have 148, 150 or 152 fusions.
- **The input was the same.** The pre-compile fingerprint matched on all ranks, and all ranks read the same autotune snapshot.

So XLA produced different fusion decisions for identical input on different processes. I don't yet know whether this is in-process nondeterminism or some per-process state. A third run (`...20261128e-i11775v5`) recompiles the same module 3 times inside each process after the mismatch and logs whether the hash is stable. If the hash varies inside one process, I'll file an upstream XLA issue with the module.

None of this changes the train-step result above: one executable on all ranks, about 47 s per step.

🤖 The eval-program mismatch is nondeterministic compilation inside one process.

In the third run (`/karan/task504-distill-1h-a-hard-20261128e-i11775v5`), each process recompiled `jit_accum_for_batch` 3 more times right after the mismatch. It used `backend_compile_and_load` directly, so the persistent cache was not involved. Each process used the same `ir.Module`, devices and compile options as its first compile.

| Processes | Distinct optimized-HLO hashes over 4 compiles in one process |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 (stable) |
| 10 | 2 |
| 30 | 3 |
| 23 | 4 |

- 63 of 64 processes produced more than one optimized HLO for the same input.
- There were 31 distinct hashes across the job.
- The hash sets overlap between processes, so the variants are a pool of fusion outcomes, not per-rank states.

So this is not Marin or Iris state, and not the autotune cache. XLA's GPU compile of this module is nondeterministic. The earlier diff places the divergence in fusion decisions for small `s32` slice/min/pad/concatenate trees, before latency-hiding scheduling.

Next: a run (`...20261128f-i11775v6`) has process 0 compile the module twice with per-pass HLO dumps. The first pass whose outputs differ will go into an upstream XLA issue, with the dumped input module as the reproducer.

For PR 12423 and PR 11923 in the meantime:
- In-job cold compiles of this eval program will fail the executable check whatever autotune data is present.
- A persistent-cache hit avoids the problem, because every rank loads process 0's executable.
- The train step's cold compile was stable across all 64 ranks in both runs. I have not tested whether its compile is stable within one process.

🤖 The eval-program nondeterminism is a known XLA bug. It is fixed upstream, but not in our jaxlib.

**Where it starts.** In `/karan/task504-distill-1h-a-hard-20261128f-i11775v6`, process 0 compiled `jit_accum_for_batch` twice with `xla_dump_hlo_pass_re=.*`. The two compiles gave different results (`82588242…` and `9763270a…`), and each wrote 201 dump files.
- The last dump before fusion, `0126 fusion.after_pipeline-start`, is byte-identical between the two compiles. The passes between it and priority fusion did not change the module.
- The first output that differs is **`0127 fusion.after_priority-fusion`**. That diff has 3,374 changed lines, all in `jit(accum_for_batch)/Transformer` slice/min/pad/concatenate/add ops.

**Upstream.** This matches openxla/xla issue 49047, "GPU compilation is not reproducible: GpuHloCostAnalysis sums float utilizations in pointer-hash order, PriorityFusion near-ties flip between processes":
- `GpuHloCostAnalysis` sums per-root utilizations over a pointer-keyed `flat_hash_set`, so the float rounding depends on heap layout.
- Near-tied fusion priorities then flip.

That fits what we see. Each compile allocates at different addresses, so even recompiles inside one process differ.

**Versions.**

| Package | XLA commit | Contains the fix |
|---|---|---|
| jaxlib 0.11.1 (Marin's CUDA pin) | `dcf304bc5d` (2026-08-17) | no, 966 commits before it |
| jax 0.12.0 | `d867969800` | yes |
| jax 0.12.1 | `97b8433b3e` | yes |

The fix is openxla/xla commit `ee21092a8a`, "Use deterministic ordering for elementwise_use_roots_ in GpuHloCostAnalysis" (2026-09-22). No new upstream issue is needed.

**What this means here.**
- The same bug can in principle hit the train step too. It compiled to one executable on all 64 ranks in both runs, but that may be because this module has no near-ties at its fusion decisions. It is not a guarantee.
- With the PR 11923 guard, any in-job cold compile that hits a near-tie fails at start-up instead of running mixed executables.
- The real fix is moving the CUDA path to jax 0.12.x, or carrying a backport of `ee21092a8a`. I have not tested a jax 0.12 GPU run.

**Summary for issue 11775.**
1. The original 3× slowdown: per-rank autotune folders, where only process 0 and the per-node fetchers had tuned data. PR 12423 with a seeded snapshot fixes this; measured steady step about 47 s on a cold compile.
2. Cross-rank executable mismatches that remain after that: the upstream PriorityFusion nondeterminism above, fixed in jax 0.12.x.

11883.body:
🤖 Holistic review of d2e5cdc2c6e7dde0289b8cd6ddd537b66ee4039e.

This change keeps the rollout record honest when `iris cluster controller restart` fails before it touches the controller. Findings 1–4 are resolved and the rollback state machine is correct on every path I traced. The remaining item is merge order with an open PR on the same Kubernetes code.

**Before.** `controller_restart` wrote `PENDING`, called `restart_controller`, and treated any exception as a failed health check. Auto-rollback then wrote `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED`. If the restart had never reached the controller (expired SSH authorization in #11879, or a missing kube prerequisite), the running controller stayed up with a checkpoint restore armed for its next unplanned boot. That restore would replace the live database with the pre-deploy checkpoint.

**Design.** `ControllerRestartNotStarted` now lives on the `ControllerProvider` protocol (`protocols.py`). Both real implementations raise it from their pre-change steps. `vm_lifecycle.restart_controller` covers GCP and manual: VM discovery, a 90-second SSH probe, and script construction all run before `GcpStandaloneWorkerHandle.bootstrap` writes `startup-script` metadata. `K8sControllerProvider.start_controller` is now split into `_prepare_controller_start`, which runs the read-only checks and resolves the storage credentials into a `_ControllerStartPreparation`, and `_apply_controller_start`. `restart_controller` wraps only the preparation step in `ControllerRestartNotStarted`. The CLI handles each path as follows:

| Path | Restart never began | Restart began and failed |
|---|---|---|
| Forward deploy | restore `prior_record` (or a `COMMITTED` record for the configured image), exit 1 | auto-rollback writes `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED` |
| Auto-rollback | restore the forward `PENDING` record with its checkpoint coordinates, exit 1 | exit 1, restore stays armed |
| `--rollback` | restore the record read at command start, exit 1 | exit 1, restore stays armed |

**Evidence and limits.** I ran the three changed test files locally: 83 passed. The CLI tests use a hand-written provider double, but the record I/O is real (`file://` rollout records), and the provider-level tests use the in-memory K8s fake and the fake VM handle. That combination covers both sides of the exception contract. No live GCE or CoreWeave restart was exercised. The design pass was done inline; no independent reviewer was launched.

**Findings**

- **5. Related PR:** #12356 (Load CoreWeave controller storage keys from Secret Manager) deletes `uses_s3_storage` and `_resolve_s3_credentials`, which `_prepare_controller_start` calls. It also replaces the credential condition with `needs_controller_storage_credentials` and resolves `controller.coreweave.storage_credentials_ref` in `preflight_controller`. When the second PR rebases, a mechanical substitution such as `resolve_controller_storage_credentials(None)` would check the operator key pair even though the cluster is configured with a Secret Manager reference. Restarts on such a cluster would then fail as "not started" whenever the operator keys are absent. Land #11883 first, so #12356 moves its credential resolution into `_prepare_controller_start` in one place. If #12356 lands first, have `_prepare_controller_start` use `needs_controller_storage_credentials(config)` and the credentials `preflight_controller` resolved from the configured reference.

Earlier findings: 4 resolved (`start_controller` and `restart_controller` share one preparation step); 1 resolved (`--rollback` restores its prior record on `ControllerRestartNotStarted`); 2 resolved (the exception is on the provider protocol and Kubernetes classifies read-only failures); 3 resolved (the forward path restores `prior_record` unchanged).

<!-- marin-holistic-review:d2e5cdc2c6e7dde0289b8cd6ddd537b66ee4039e -->

🤖 @weaverbot review of this PR: the logic is correct and both resolved threads are genuinely addressed. Please fix these small items, then rebase on main (PR 11841 touched `k8s/controller.py`):
1. When auto-rollback cannot begin, `_rollback_controller` re-raises `ControllerRestartNotStarted` inside `controller_restart`'s `except Exception`, so the user gets a traceback instead of the clean `SystemExit(1)`. Catch it in `_auto_rollback` (the record is already restored) and exit cleanly.
2. The k8s pre-check resolves S3 credentials only when `uses_s3_storage`, but `start_controller` also resolves them when `node_health.storage` is set. Mirror that condition, so a credential failure counts as "restart never started".
3. Raise the new SSH probe timeout from 30 s to about 90 s. `start_controller` waits 300 s, and a 30 s probe will fail restarts on slow `gcloud compute ssh`.

When the second PR rebases, a mechanical substitution such as `resolve_controller_storage_credentials(None)` would check the operator key pair even though the cluster is configured with a Secret Manager reference. Restarts on such a cluster would then fail as "not started" whenever the operator keys are absent. Land #11883 first with finding 4 applied, so #12356 updates one preparation step. If #12356 lands first, have this PR's precheck call `needs_controller_storage_credentials(config)` and rely on `preflight_controller` for the configured reference.

<!-- marin-holistic-followup:0e41b777edc96bb0a213542e39366eec7ceede2f -->

🤖 Addressed the [new holistic review](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11883#issuecomment-7232562110) in [d2e5cdc2c6](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/d2e5cdc2c6). Kubernetes start and restart now share one read-only preparation step for scale-group validation, controller secrets, prerequisites, and storage credentials. Restart classifies failures from that step as `ControllerRestartNotStarted`; the apply phase uses the prepared values without repeating the checks. This gives #12356 one credential-preparation path to update when it rebases.

The three original follow-ups remain addressed: failed automatic rollback exits cleanly, node-health storage credentials are resolved before Kubernetes changes, and the VM SSH probe allows 90 seconds. The branch is rebased on current main, including #11841.

Changed-file lint and Pyrefly passed. After the refactor, the focused Kubernetes, CLI, and VM tests passed (83 tests); the renamed CLI scenarios passed again (7 tests). The earlier full Iris run recorded 3,114 passes and one xdist worker crash, and that crashed test passed in an isolated rerun. The broad local selector was limited by its missing `pytest-asyncio` plugin and session timeout. CI passed on d2e5cdc2c6, including Iris unit tests and the CoreWeave smoke check.

issue.title: [rl] Turn-deadline expiry discards partial generations as zero-token rollouts
issue.body:
Mochi .129 archives can report `generated_tokens=0` when a turn deadline cancels a long active decode before a complete non-streaming ModelTurn reaches the recorder. This does not establish that the inference engine generated no tokens. The original blanket engine-queue-starvation diagnosis was unsupported.

The balanced 500-rollout sample contains 58 such timeout rows (11.6%). In the learner's separate consumed-batch cohort, 363/12,800 rows were verifier-unavailable (2.84%); they were token-loss masked and excluded from RLOO baselines, not trained as reward-zero failures.

Retained timing events match 29 of the 58 sampled session IDs and cover 32 request IDs with 115–19,735 generated tokens. Internal queue wait was at most 18.529 s and first-token delay at most 19.773 s. Last observed decode spans reach 1,743.155 s (median 1,291.646 s), mostly from progress events rather than completed requests. These aggregates include three sessions outside a coarse timing check. Session reuse, Ray log suppression and unobserved pre-engine waits prevent a strict causal fraction for all 58 rows. No retained event demonstrates an engine admission wait approaching 1,800 s; the overall queue-starvation share remains unknown.

The same run's step-24 Micro210 evaluation originally scored 365/434 trials. The existing BixBench regrade brings that to 375/434; the user authorized recovery of only the remaining 58 no-response slots and one verifier timeout, keeping all 375 graded outcomes unchanged.

Private sample: `open-athena/mochi-rl-129-rollout-sample`, `rollouts.parquet`, e.g. `transcripts/0125.md`. Run record: marin-community/marin-logbooks#88. Evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-zero-token-timeouts/2026.11.26.1/deadline-correction-evidence.json`.

Expected: retain the exact partial generation when an active decode reaches its deadline and run the real verifier under #10197. A genuinely never-scheduled request must use a distinct bounded admission allowance. Output length and slow decode under load need separate attribution.

Done when:

- Active deadline expiry returns exact sampled tokens, behavior logprobs, routes and policy-step stamps for verification, without a synthetic EOS or a fabricated completed response. Apply the contract to canonical evaluation as well as future authored Mochi RL recipes.
- Preserve the user's slot-ownership-clock requirement: execution budgets start/resume at actual engine scheduling, with a saturated-slot regression. This is a guard against real admission wait, not an established explanation of the sampled cohort.
- Report queue wait separately from generation time, and attribute slow decode with per-request/per-engine evidence rather than inferring it from a zero-token archive.
- Confirm unavailable rows are excluded from token loss and RLOO baselines. This masking check is complete.

Partial-retention implementation 0602a5bbdc is landed and enabled by future Mochi RL recipes; admission-clock implementation e6aeaa1813/1802d95806 is landed through 77f3e5f57a. Already submitted jobs remain pinned. Shared task-client partial return is now landed in 36098e90e2, covering future canonical evaluation without a protocol override. The already submitted exact-59 recovery remains on 77f3. GPU runtime certification and slow-decode attribution remain open.

issue.title: [experiment] Reduce Mochi SFT doom loops with online FTPO
issue.body:
## TL;DR

Measure exact repetitive tails in Mochi SFT step 400407, then test whether online FTPO can halve per-domain incidence while retaining native task correctness. Baseline measurement precedes training.

## Description

Adapt the [Dr. Doom campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) to Mochi. Preserve the exact tail-loop detector and FTPO objective. Use TP1/BF16 serving and Mochi's MuonH/R3 training path. The fixed, hashed evaluation panel covers math, instruction following, coding, reasoning_gym, structured outputs, and STEM MCQ. All graders are programmatic and fail closed.

## Hypothesis or Goal

For each target domain, obtain a post-training loop upper bound no greater than half its confirmed baseline count on identical prompts. Extend low-incidence 32K cohorts from 128 to 256; fewer than 10 confirmed loops after extension makes a domain non-target. Non-target upper bounds may increase by at most three. Per-domain correctness may lose at most max(3, 5% of N) passes; pooled correctness may lose at most 2% of the panel.

## Status

Native-rendered cohort v2 is published and verified (manifest SHA-256 `1c2f2b83a3b895b518e7745d3a1fe05af857f56273449c6a3aad9087f9354af3`). Corrected S0 was submitted November 24 at 19:45:04 EST, runtime `2026.11.24.4`, source `1661a15e9f`, for 128 GB200 on cw-us-east-08a at production priority. Coordinator and GPU child are running. No valid incidence count is available yet; training remains pending.

The first S0 attempt was cancelled at 19:25 EST because preparation omitted the native answer-format instruction when hashing prompts. Its outputs and v1 hash table are excluded. V2 exactly matches the saved native prompt; all 512 original math tasks remain eligible.

Seal the full baseline and sparse-domain reserves before S1. The executor clock remains November 24 17:46 EST through November 26 17:46 EST; start no training after November 26 13:46 EST.

## Links

- Prior campaign: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691
- Source branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo
- Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/codex/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/logbooks/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/notebook.md

## Decision Log

- Freeze baseline prompts and detector before choosing target domains.
- Keep circular but nonperiodic reasoning out of the exact-loop objective; report length stops and open reasoning spans separately.

## Conclusion

Pending measurement.

issue.title: [long-loop] Ablate the RL optimizer and learning rate for Mochi and Snowball
issue.body:
Mochi and Snowball long-loop RL need an ablated optimizer and learning rate. Since the 2026-11-23 normalization, both models use MuonH with `lr` 1e-5 and `adam_lr` 2.307692307692308e-6 (`offload_momentum: true`), `max_grad_norm` 0.5 and 64 prompts × 8 samples per batch. Snowball moved from AdamW to MuonH for memory: AdamW state did not fit at long context without CPU optimizer offload, and offload slowed each step. Neither the optimizer nor the learning rate came from an ablation. The earlier tuned Snowball RL comparison in #7786 (hypothesis V) found that AdamW learned faster and reached a higher peak training reward than MuonH. This experiment should settle both choices for each model. It is planned here and not yet scheduled.

Design:
- Curriculum: our best RL curriculum at the time it runs, identical for both models. Record its identity and version.
- Fixed settings: the normalized config for all other settings (staleness 3, 98,304-token response cap and 131,072-token context, batch 64 × 8, `max_grad_norm` 0.5), one seed per arm, and the frozen 200-row validation split from the curriculum.
- Optimizer arms: (a) MuonH with `offload_momentum: true` and the `adam_lr`/`lr` ratio held fixed; (b) AdamW with CPU optimizer offload. Each arm uses the qualified trainer layout for its memory profile.
- Grid per optimizer and model: half-decade steps. MuonH starts at 3e-6, 1e-5, 3e-5 and 1e-4. AdamW starts at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5. Learning rates do not transfer between optimizers.
- Metric: an EMA of validation accuracy over the first 20 optimizer updates (EMA window 5, matching best-checkpoint selection). Report raw per-eval accuracy and training reward alongside it.
- Cost: report median seconds per update and GPU-hours per update for each arm, split into rollout wait, optimizer step and offload transfer. AdamW with offload wins only if its accuracy gain justifies its step-time cost.
- Adaptive grid: if the best arm of an optimizer is at either edge of its grid, add the next half-decade step beyond that edge and repeat until the best value is interior.
- Stability checks per arm: training/inference mismatch KL, gradient norm and the clipped-gradient fraction. Report any divergence as a result, not a rerun.

Done when:
- Each optimizer has a learning-rate curve per model whose best value is interior to its grid, with EMA validation accuracy at 20 updates and seconds per update per arm.
- A recommended optimizer and learning rate per model is stated, with the accuracy, cost and stability metrics that support it.
- The long-loop RL defaults are updated, or confirmed unchanged, from that recommendation.

issue.title: [curation] Polaris grader rejects correct Mochi and plain-text answers
issue.body:
Polaris's retained TaskSpecs request plain-text answers, but the packaged grader requires literal `</think>` followed by a boxed result. Correct plain-text answers and Mochi's `<|end_think|>` output therefore receive scored reward 0 with nonzero token-loss masks. This is a mismatch between the retained task/consumer contract and the intentionally preserved upstream format gate, not a failure of the mathematical equality check.

Two independent blinded reviews of 20 retained responses from Mochi campaign runs `.532` and `.534` agreed on 17 correct final answers and 3 missing finals. All 20 received 0. The larger retained population has 202/202 zeros; it has not been independently regraded.

Reproduce:

1. Extract the [frozen audit bundle](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-rl-data-campaign%2Fpolaris-audit%2F2026.11.26.1%2Faudit-evidence.tar.gz). Install its pinned Sympy 1.13.3, pylatexenc 2.10 and mpmath 1.3.0.
2. From the extracted directory, run:

```python
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "frozen-grader")
from grade import score
contract = json.load(open("cases/P-2-06/config.json"))
assert score("63", contract) == 0
assert score(r"\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<|start_think|>work<|end_think|>\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<think>work</think>\boxed{63}", contract) == 1
```

The same contrast reproduces for correct answers `12000` and `6` on two other tasks. Incorrect, empty and unfinished-reasoning controls return 0. This CPU repro calls the unchanged `score` function used by the CLI; local `/app` and `/tests` placement was not exercised.

Expected: the grader/binding accepts a mathematically correct answer in the task's advertised format across supported model reasoning protocols, while preserving wrong-answer and incomplete-output failures. It must not impose an undisclosed XML or boxing requirement.

Affected retained source: `open-athena/polaris-project-polaris-dataset-53k-b25e0cb8-retained-20261116-b-v1@9079512fe3d2d332b446b1b37deb9d2898f5461e`; upstream scorer revision `eda12fe22dd83aca59ec46a67147240dc483f62b`. Producer files are `experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/polaris/grade.py` and `tasks.py` on the ingestion branch. Fix forward on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` with a regression and re-seal/re-pin for future rounds. Existing campaign runs and records remain unchanged.

[Contract frozen before code inspection](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/91#issuecomment-7207765866). The bundle includes exact scripts, fixtures, dependency lock, sample selection and independent reviews. Storage: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-rl-data-campaign/polaris-audit/2026.11.26.1/audit-evidence.tar.gz`.

comments.body:
🤖 I ran the v4 grader over all 53,291 rows of POLARIS-53K. It raises on 1,433 of them, and 397 of those have a valid choice-label reference. It also cannot pay the correct answer in its natural form when the reference ends in a factorial (70 rows) or contains a negation word (12 rows).

Setup: `score` from `polaris_repair.grader_files()` at `334094a731`, called in process on `polaris-data-53K.jsonl` at `296f8e3413`, with math-verify 0.9.0, latex2sympy2-extended 1.11.0 and sympy 1.13.3. The config is `{"problem", "answer"}`, as the converter writes it. The first reply for each row is its own reference in a box. Line numbers count from 0.

**Rows that raise**

| raise | rows |
|---|---:|
| `InvalidTask`: math-verify cannot parse the reference | 926 |
| `InvalidTask`: "Polaris reference label and choice content disagree" | 421 |
| `InvalidTask`: "Polaris reference names an undeclared choice" | 62 |
| `InvalidTask`: "the reference parses to an undefined value" | 22 |
| `GradingInfraError`: "math verifier deadline exhausted" | 2 |

On 1,411 of the 1,433, the replies `0`, `x+1` and an empty reply raise as well. The retained release keeps 53,167 of the 53,291 rows, so at least 1,309 of the 1,433 are in the release that `source_pins.json` binds. I cannot read the release to count them exactly.

475 of the raising rows have a reference that starts with `\textbf{(X)}` for a choice the question declares. In 397 of them the text after the label is empty, or equals the declared choice once LaTeX spacing and the backslash left by a lost `\ ` are removed:

- Line 48 stores `\textbf{(D)}\20\sqrt{2}`, and choice D is `\ 20\sqrt{2}`. `math_reference` compares `\20\sqrt{2}` with the choice and raises for `D`, `20\sqrt{2}` and `\boxed{20\sqrt{2}}`.
- Line 2540 stores `\textbf{(E)}`, and choice E is `\ -1`. `E`, `-1` and `\boxed{-1}` raise.

As a check I made `math_reference` return the declared choice for those 397 rows. 341 then grade as expected: the label and the boxed choice score 1, and every other label scores 0. The other 56 have choices the comparator cannot handle, mostly sentences: 48 still raise, and 8 grade a reply wrongly.

21 of the 22 undefined references are times on the hour, such as `3:00` (line 2414) and `6:00 \text{ P.M.}`, which parse to `zoo`.

**Correct answers that score 0**

- 71 references end in `!`: `n!` on 22 rows, `10!`, `(2n-1)!!`. `final_candidate` removes the factorial sign with `rstrip(".!")` (`polaris_grade.py` L165). On 68 of them the reference scores 0 bare, in `\boxed{}` and as "The answer is n!.", and 1 only inside `$…$`. On 2 more it exhausts the verifier deadline; these are the two deadline rows above. With `rstrip(".")`, 70 of the 71 score 1 in all of those forms.
- 12 references match `NEGATION` (L152), so `final_candidate` returns no candidate for a reply that states them: `False` (3 rows), `\text{Not guilty}`, `Not\ Equivalent`, `will \ not`, and 6 sentences with "not". Each scores 0 in every form I tried. The 10 rows whose reference is `True` score 1 for `True`.

A labelled reference with a lost space can also pass the agreement check. Line 34241 stores `\textbf{(C)}\y^{2}+10y-7=0`, and the labels A, B and D score 1 as well as C.

## TL;DR

A week-long ablation over RL data mixtures on Mochi. Each candidate mix of 4–8 Atlas sources at equal weight trains for 50 RL steps with the RL config of run `.131` held fixed. The user-authorized 2026-11-27 protocol drops validation for new launches and makes the final checkpoint the Micro210 deliverable; earlier runs retain their documented protocol history. Three runs go at a time. Results are being collected.

## Description

The RL config is fixed at that of `long-loop-mochi-exp4-dspark-rl-2026.11.25.131`: DSpark, 144 GB200 = 64 trainer (PP16/CP4/TP1/EP4) + 80 rollout, TP1/BF16, and the .131 initializer. The documented protocol changes below apply alongside the equal-weight curriculum mix (1/k per source). Each run is 50 optimizer steps with no wall-clock budget. A run stops early only when it is clearly broken, for example a data defect, all-zero rewards or a grader error storm.

Every mix has at least 2 SWE/agentic families and at least 2 competition-math families. Every source has at least 500 tasks. Sources Mochi had already saturated at the start of RL are left out (nemotron_if, openscience). The candidates come from the holiday Atlas burndown (marin #12329): v2 has 50 mixes and v3 has 50 more.

The queue follows human priority ratings: High, then Medium, then Low. Mixes with a source whose stored grader predates fixes on main run after all clean mixes, until those sources are re-sealed. Mixes run as listed, including sources that are Pending in the served R40 catalog, at their declared pins. Each run records which of its sources diverge from the catalog.

## Protocol changes

- **Stall-stop cutover, 2026-11-26:** new launches use the repeat-stall guard at `f163b89b94` or later, qualified at `ef09a1e250`. Existing `.532`, `.534` and `.540` retain their earlier running configurations. Record the cutover per run; it changes comparability.
- **Validation dropped, final checkpoint is the deliverable, user-authorized 2026-11-27 (11:15 EST).** New launches have no holdout validation, no validation evaluations and no best-by-val selection. Export the last checkpoint and evaluate it with canonical Micro210. The frozen Micro210 scoring and coverage policy remains unchanged.
- **Checkpoint policy, user-authorized 2026-11-27 (11:16 EST):** save every five steps, retain at most two rolling checkpoints (latest plus one previous resume fallback), and always save the final step. Finished-run retention is the final checkpoint plus inputs still read by pending evals; prune everything else.
- **Effective from:** mix-009 `.712`, root `/benfeuer/mochi-campaign-v2-mix-009-2026.11.27.712`, submission receipt **2026-11-27 17:23:27 UTC**, source `6c915ab36edfa1da764471acf9c1d7eed645d426`. This is the first accepted RL root under the no-validation/final-checkpoint/interval5/keep2 policy. Its regional real-agent gate and GPU admission remain pending; submission is not a training-result claim. The prior `.711` failed before training and remains historical.
- **Existing-run selection:** use final step50 for `.532` and `.534`. Do not restart or change `.540`'s running config; after it finishes, export/evaluate its final checkpoint and ignore its best-by-val selection. While it runs, preserve its current best and latest as directed for the immediate storage pass.
- Mark this protocol era alongside stall-stop in every result comparison. Earlier validation-trained runs and later no-validation runs are not interchangeable controls.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find which data sources and mixtures improve Mochi most per RL step, on final-checkpoint Micro210 and training reward curves, with protocol eras recorded. Then use that to choose the RL data mix for the next long-loop runs.

## Status

The run table is authoritative. Production RL coordinators for mix-009 `.712` and v3-mix-014 `.713` were accepted with landed source `6c915ab36e`. Their full-population pools and serial candidate native checks passed. Regional real-agent/credential admission and GPU startup are pending; no training result is claimed. `.712` is the first submitted coordinator configured for the no-validation/final-checkpoint/interval5/keep2 protocol. issue.title: [experiment] Measure Mochi action loops and loop guards
issue.body:
## TL;DR

No tested guard met the complete registered loop-reduction rule. **S1-stop came closest:** it missed only TBLite's 50% bar, achieving **42.5%**, and correctness passes under the user's **×0.75 override**.

## Status

**Closed as completed on November 26, 2026, under the final user disposition.** All measured runs, audits and required conservation are complete. No registered repeat remains. **I4 is UNPERFORMED** because its required pinned 216-store manifest is unavailable; **no follow-up run**. No exports, new compute or deletions; conserved artifacts remain unchanged.

## Conclusion

S1-stop, repetition penalty and antithrash RL after four updates each fail their registered loop gates. Correctness passes the user-reduced thresholds. **I3 remains FAIL + UNDERPOWERED:** treatment logged zero antithrash fire fraction and mean penalty at every update, so this pair does not establish the efficacy or causal harm of actively applied antithrash. The experiment is closed with these negative results and limitations.

[Final notebook and user disposition](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b84d32f6f7e5c587f4c3ed4a14e1efbcef52fc5e/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/notebook.md). [Index PR #87](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/pull/87) is ready for review; validation passes and the coordinator will merge it.

## Recorded protocol and results

Can Mochi action loops be cut by at least 50% while holding correctness? S0 is sealed. Both inference guards and fixed-N4 antithrash RL fail their registered loop gates. Under the November 26 **user override** lowering correctness thresholds by 25%, both guards pass correctness. The RP repeat no longer has a registered trigger and was canceled; its root and GPU child are verified killed.

The **user override** extending every recorded clock by 24 hours restores antithrash I3. T0 remains November 25 12:01:36 EST; T20 is November 27 08:01:36, T32 November 27 20:01:36, and the deadline November 28 12:01:36 EST. N=4 updates is fixed for both S2 arms before submission, based on the existing conservative seven-hour update budget plus three hours for startup. The initial revision3 pair failed before training on the NVML output-pointer defect. Revision4 is accepted from pushed source `ecc9fb1bae`, which also uses main's valid Ray fabric-label encoding. Control accepted November26 13:51:23.963 EST and treatment13:51:46.099 EST. Both passed physical placement. Control entered the training loop at14:08:51.538 EST and treatment at14:09:04.855 EST, before extended T20. Initial policy synchronization completed for both. Treatment optimizer step1 is verified at14:49:17.976 EST (256 consumed samples and702,668 loss tokens), followed by policy synchronization at14:49:24.739 EST. Both fixed-N4 training arms SUCCEEDED on immutable source `ecc9fb1bae`: treatment16:07:30.092 EST/control16:23:47.809 EST, each checkpoint4/all15 GPU tasks succeeded0fail/preempt. S2x is complete: both converters SUCCEEDED/all12 tasks and permanent regional models verified, each221 files/215 shards/56,504 tensors/1,070,983,169,596 recorded bytes. Header/size checks and conservation-marker readbacks passed; no payload rehash, automatic pruning enforcement unverified. The S3 pair was submitted once per arm from clean `cc4e3dcc62`/tree `22ae5b80cc`, revision2026.11.26.1: control17:28:51.657 EST (coordinator suffix9e9f6a58, attempta80899aa9a3f), treatment17:29:23.641 (dd65e4e6, a9599be43c43). Each64GB200/723 frozen trials, production08a/all racks,128total after both converters released. Both S3 roots and all16 GPU tasks per arm SUCCEEDED with zero Iris failures/preemptions; all723 rollouts returned per arm and final dumps were verified. Both once-per-arm CPU postprocessors also SUCCEEDED: audit, verified permanent trace conservation and saved-report refresh complete,42evaluations/no reporting error per arm. I3 is **FAIL; no registered repeat trigger**. Repeat-turn shares control→treatment are TB2 .1501067499→.2138755238 (+42.48%), TBLite .0765120233→.0814704421 (+6.48%) and held-out .1321535607→.2021508130 (+52.97%). None meet the registered50% cut. The paired I3 run is also underpowered under its preregistered diagnostic: treatment logged antithrash fire fraction0 and mean penalty0 at every consumed update1–4, confirmed in W&B and native records despite enabled correct_only/0.02/cap0.1 config. No retuning; N remained4. This does not establish efficacy or causal harm of actively applied antithrash. [Exposure decision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/998731571f/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s2-antithrash-exposure-decision-20261126.json). Correctness passes original and user-overridden gates: passes236→235 pooled; overridden concurrent-control cohort floors28.9875/48.75/72.15, pooled166.155. Assessed counts700/723 control and693/723 treatment; every cohort>=90%, zero unavailable outputs. Frozen cohort hashes match both arms and S0; S0 remains report-only for I3. [Paired decision and no-repeat receipt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/fc2ace0d05/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s3-i3-paired-verdict-20261126.json). Saved configs bind each verified step4 export and frozen protocol:BF16/TP1/DP16/EP16, eagerfalse, seed20261125, temperature0.7/top_p1/RP1, stops128001/128009, main_generate. All registered S3 roots/children and CPU postprocessors completed; measured-arm verdicts are recorded. Initial local credential check failed before submission; documented dedicated eval key resolved it. The4.29TB resumable-step1 copy is complete and permanently conserved; its superseded temporary source was deleted under the storage directive. No further Hub copies. [S3 submission receipt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c9c580bfaf/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s3-pair-submission.json). A frozen partial task-health snapshot contains500/513 graded receipt attempts for control and503/515 for treatment, with3/9 ConnectionErrors respectively. These incomplete receipt sets do not establish the consumed batch's masking rate or a treatment effect. [Snapshot and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5142a50aef/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s2-r4-task-health-snapshot-1505.json). Consolidation `27a544e838` was adopted after loop entry, with cleanup `71297b9d15`; required lint and24 affected safe tests passed. [Revision4 receipt and notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/19bdb873ec/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/notebook.md).

## Design

The frozen S0 panel has 823 trials: TB2 89×3, TBLite 100×2, SWE100 100×1 and SWESmith held-out 128×2. Follow-up arms retain 723 trials after the budget drop registered before baseline outcomes; SWE100 remains baseline-only. Held-out row hashes are excluded from the RL pool. Every arm initializes from Mochi SFT step400407 because the predecessor [Dr Doom experiment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12240) produced no gain.

Action loops are the frozen stall/run8/frequent/terminus8 rules. Loop UB is confirmed looping trials plus unassessed trials. Infrastructure outcomes are excluded from correctness under [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197), and each cohort needs at least 90% valid trials.

The stall stop must halve repeat-turn share on every target cohort; repetition penalty1.1 must reduce action-loop UB to no more than half S0's confirmed count. Antithrash applies a0.02 penalty per repeated action, capped at0.1, only to otherwise-correct trajectories; its paired primary measure is repeat-turn share, [registered before baseline results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12264#issuecomment-7171525899). Both S2 arms keep stall stopping off and share seed, pool, LR, allocation and initializer. Each requests60 GB200 (48policy+12inference), production priority on08a, all racks, TP1/BF16 with CUDA graphs enabled.

## Evidence

[Corrected S0 seal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12264#issuecomment-7190461858): 796/823 assessed,27 infrastructure,0 unavailable, all cohorts valid. The original v9/v10 controls remain invalid because saved feedback was lost; v12 replaces them.

| Cohort | Assessed/N | Confirmed action loops | Action UB | Repeat-turn share | Passes | Target |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TB2 |250/267|34|51|0.1192787795|54|Yes|
| TBLite |194/200|20|26|0.0974277259|66|Yes|
| SWE100 |99/100|3|4|0.0466101695|52|No; baseline-only|
| Held-out |253/256|13|16|0.1216524559|117|Yes|

The registered blinded precision review found29 genuine stalls among30 fires (96.67%, exceeding90%). The one false fire remains; no detector retuning or resampling.

Both original S1 arms completed all723 trials, with retained traces and matching frozen cohort hashes. [Stop result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12264#issuecomment-7195556024), [RP result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12264#issuecomment-7197268511).

| Arm/cohort | Assessed/N | Repeat-turn share | Action UB | Passes | Unchanged primary gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Stop TB2 |252/267|0.0481669267|45|59|Pass:59.62% cut|
| Stop TBLite |197/200|0.0560357675|16|69|Fail:42.48% cut|
| Stop held-out |247/256|0.0066515250|25|101|Pass:94.53% cut|
| RP TB2 |257/267|0.1654309546|46|61|Fail:cap17|
| RP TBLite |194/200|0.0680948738|16|70|Fail:cap10|
| RP held-out |250/256|0.1742603920|24|103|Fail:raw cap6.5|

**User override: correctness ×0.75.** Original raw correctness minima40.65/56/104.2 and pooled222.54 become30.4875/42/78.15 and pooled166.905 (display166.9; integer minima31/42/79/167). Stop passes59/69/101 pooled229; RP61/70/103 pooled234. Both now pass all correctness gates. Originally, held-out correctness failed in both arms; RP103 was within±2 of104.2 and triggered a repeat. Under the override, no target correctness or action-UB threshold is within±2. The repeat supplies no replacement result. Loop and validity gates remain unchanged.

Thus stop remains FAIL because of TBLite's loop reduction, and RP remains FAIL on all three action-UB gates. Original and recomputed receipts are preserved side by side in the [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/da0f50514a/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/notebook.md).

## Checkpoint conservation

**Superseding user override: the SFT checkpoint may remain PUBLIC.** Current conservation is the public sealed `open-athena/Marin-Mochi-535B-A23B@sft-fullab-v2-step-400407`, commit `cfc315a0dcd12d8be5eb0023c0693c435af98998`, plus the permanent never-prune08a source. Retained verification covers206 HF files,199 common model files and193 weight shards, with all index shards present. Weight hashes use the retained verified regional inventory; no new model download or weight rehash was performed.

The coordinator inbox entries labeled15:25/15:30 EST relay the user's public-conservation decision and confirm that the coordinator deleted the separate1.07TB private copy. This supersedes the earlier private-copy requirement and receipts. This lane did not delete it. **Make no more HF copies.** The regional permanent marker and canonical conservation receipt now reference the public sealed revision and preserve never-prune retention; automatic sweep enforcement remains unverified.

[Current user-override receipt and correction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/defde703b3/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/sft-400407-public-conservation-user-override.json). Treatment step1's original regional verified-copy job SUCCEEDED with zero failures/preemptions, observed19:47:43 EST. Its completion manifest contains59 data files/4,292,558,588,036bytes; every path, size, SHA-256 and source identity matches staging. Manifest SHA256 `e212783fc5f64836448548bde420402320ad93d764039050f47085595e8fedab`. The permanent destination has60objects including its manifest; its permanent/exclude-every-sweep marker passed byte readback. Automatic sweep enforcement remains unverified. [Conservation receipt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/e42e165ab3/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s2-treatment-step1-conservation-complete.json). Historical private-HF receipt remains superseded/deleted; no further HF operation.

After successful conservation, the obsolete temporary step1 source was removed and post-delete verified. Cumulative S2 temporary-checkpoint cleanup is8prefixes/472objects/**34,339,242,608,088 logical bytes**. Both checkpoint roots now contain only one-byte metadata markers. Permanent checkpoint, step4 exports, SFT400407, non-checkpoint evidence and all S3 outputs/scratch remain intact. Region-wide free capacity was not measured. [Original seven-prefix manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/e42e165ab3/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/storage-cleanup-20261126.json), [post-copy source-retirement manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/e42e165ab3/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/storage-step1-source-retirement-20261126.json).

Postprocessing source `8939ee19df` requires an explicit regional frozen manifest; canonical/file hashes and published task IDs/order match sealed S0. Comparison source7191758004 is pushed; required lint and33focused tests pass. Nine Harbor failures independently reproduce on clean main underPython3.12; later broad Marin groups were not run. Both CPU postprocessors were submitted after terminal-job/final-dump verification. [Terminal and submission receipt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4367acbfad/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s3-terminal-cpu-submissions-2030.json). [Readiness receipt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/e42e165ab3/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/analysis/user-overrides-20261126/s3-postprocessing-readiness-20261126.json). Loop-guards issue updates go to#86 only.


## Final disposition and links

- [Marin tracking issue #12264](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12264).
- [Research branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/codex/86-mochi-loop-guards); final notebook commit `b84d32f6f7`.

A dated completion404 does not establish absence of other evaluations; anonymous null W&B means unknown.
